sections.content: You know *por ejemplo* from A2 Unit 30. It gives one example of a general statement. Spanish has three more ways to do the work of an example. *Como* ("such as") lists examples inside a sentence, with no comma before the noun. *Así* at the start of a sentence, followed by a comma, introduces a case that shows the point you have just made. *En concreto* ("specifically") is different: it does not give one of many, it names the exact thing you mean.

sections.title: Examples and the exact point
rows: Hay muchas formas de ahorrar. Por ejemplo, puedes cocinar en casa.
There are many ways to save. For example, you can cook at home.
Me gustan las frutas como la manzana y la pera.
I like fruit such as apples and pears.
Hay muchas formas de ahorrar. Así, puedes comprar menos y cocinar en casa.
There are many ways to save. For instance, you can buy less and cook at home.
Quiero hablar del transporte; en concreto, del autobús.
I want to talk about transport; specifically, about the bus.

sections.content: This *como* means "such as", not "as" or "since". After *en concreto* comes the one thing you mean, so you do not follow it with a list.
